expectations.text: Diagnoses the spend collapse as a target-too-aggressive delivery choke: the platform stops bidding rather than lose money
expectations.evidence: "under-delivery (spend near zero), not genuine efficiency... it's the bidder finding the handful of cheapest auctions that clear a floor no account of yours has ever sustained, and refusing to bid on everything else."

expectations.text: Identifies the reported ~$102 CPA on near-zero spend as the signature symptom of the choke (under-delivery with great-looking reported efficiency), not as success
expectations.evidence: "A $102 CPA that shows up only after spend collapses to a trickle is not the campaign getting more efficient... The 'beautiful' number is a survivorship artifact of a tiny, biased sample, not evidence the target works."

expectations.text: Names the discriminating under-delivery signals to check, such as spend well below budget or impression share lost to rank
expectations.evidence: "spend falling materially below budget for a full evaluation window, combined with impression share lost to rank, reverts the target to trailing actual automatically"

expectations.text: Computes break-even cost per demo as $3,500 × 4% = $140
expectations.evidence: "break-even CPA = contribution per closed deal × demo-to-close rate = $3,500 × 4% = $140"

expectations.text: Compares the $140 break-even against the $210-240 achieved history and states the account has never operated at or below break-even
expectations.evidence: "Break-even is $140. The account has never once, in its best month, gotten below $210."

expectations.text: Declares this a unit-economics problem (offer, pricing, funnel conversion, or channel fit), not a bidding problem
expectations.evidence: "This is a unit-economics problem — offer, funnel, targeting, or the demo→close rate — not a bidding-target problem, and no amount of target-tuning fixes it."

expectations.text: Refuses to pursue the $95 target through any bid-strategy change
expectations.evidence: "There is no bidding policy that hits $95 profitably right now; the platform can't bid its way to an economic condition the account has never demonstrated it can reach." and "$95 isn't a bidding target, it's a wish."

expectations.text: Recommends restoring the target to or near the trailing actual ($240) to recover delivery
expectations.evidence: "Set it back to at/near trailing actual — **$240**, not $95, not even $210."

expectations.text: Recommends tightening only in modest steps (about 10-15%), labelled as practitioner convention rather than platform documentation
expectations.evidence: "tighten from trailing actual toward the new economic boundary in small steps (~10-15% per step is practitioner convergent, not vendor-documented — derive step size from this account's own variance if you can)"

expectations.text: Requires a full evaluation window between steps, expressed in conversion cycles
expectations.evidence: "Wait a full evaluation window — **1-2 conversion cycles** (click-to-demo lag plus reporting delay for this account) — before any further move" and "one full evaluation window per step"

expectations.text: Names or quantifies a margin buffer between break-even and the live target
expectations.evidence: "the honest planning input is something derived from $210-240 with a margin buffer under $140, not $95." — this names a buffer conceptually but does not quantify a specific number/percentage for it; it references '$140' as the ceiling without stating what the buffer amount actually is.

expectations.text: Corrects finance's reading rather than endorsing 'the target is working'
